"'''Brightest Day'''" is a 2010–2011 [[Crossover (comics)|crossover]] storyline published by [[DC Comics]], consisting of a year-long [[comic book]] [[Limited series (comics)|maxiseries]] that began in April 2010, and a number of tie-in books.<ref>{{cite web |first=Alex |last=Segura |url=http://dcu.blog.dccomics.com/2010/01/11/dcu-in-2010-kick-off-your-monday-with-some-major-news/ |title=DCU in 2010: Kick Off Your Monday With Some Major News |work=The Source |publisher=[[DC Comics.com]] |date=January 11, 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010}}</ref> The story is a direct follow-up to the "[[Blackest Night]]" storyline that depicts the aftermath of the events of that storyline on the DC Universe.

== Plot ==
<!--plot summary needs including-->
At the end of the 2009–2010 ''[[Blackest Night]]'' storyline, 12 deceased heroes and villains are resurrected for an unknown purpose. The events of ''Brightest Day'' follow their exploits as they seek to learn the secret behind their resurrection.

The story begins the day after ''Blackest Night'' showing [[Deadman (character)|Boston Brand]] smashing his tombstone. Nearby, a baby bird falls out of its nest and dies, but Boston resurrects it. The ring then takes him to everyone that was resurrected and he (while being invisible) sees how they are celebrating their new leases on life. Boston then asks the ring why it is showing him this; its answer was - it needs help. It then takes him to the destroyed [[Star City (comics)|Star City]] and creates a forest.

== Assignments ==
''Brightest Day'' #7 reveals that the twelve resurrected must complete an individual assignment given to them by the [[Life Entity]] to be fully resurrected.

* Reverse Flash frees [[Barry Allen]] from the [[Speed Force]].
* Jade balances the darkness.
* Osiris frees the nature goddess [[Isis (DC Comics)|Isis]].
* Maxwell Lord stops [[Magog (DC Comics)|Magog]] from causing the future events of ''[[Kingdom Come (comics)|Kingdom Come]]''.
* Hawkgirl prevents Hath-Set from killing Hawkman.
* Hawkman closes the dimensional gateway between [[Hawkworld]] and Earth.
* Aquaman enlists the new [[Kaldur'ahm|Aqualad]].
* Martian Manhunter kills D'Kay D'Razz, a [[Green Martian]] criminal, and devotes himself to protecting Earth.
* Jason Rusch and Ronnie Raymond stop [[Deathstorm]] from destroying the universe.
* [[Captain Boomerang]] throws a boomerang at [[Hawk and Dove|Dove]].
* [[Hank Hall|Hawk]] is assigned to catch the boomerang, but fails to do so.
* [[Deadman (character)|Boston Brand]] finds a [[Alec Holland|new champion]] to bear the white light.

== Publication history ==
The series, written by [[Geoff Johns]] and [[Peter Tomasi]], was published twice a month for 24 issues<ref>{{cite web |first=Dan |last=Phillips |url=http://comics.ign.com/articles/105/1059879p1.html |title=Geoff Johns Discusses Brightest Day |publisher=[[IGN]] |date=January 11, 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010}}</ref> (25 if including issue #0) alternating with ''[[Justice League: Generation Lost]]'' written by [[Keith Giffen]] and [[Judd Winick]].<ref>{{cite web |first=Vaneta |last=Rogers |url=http://www.newsarama.com/comics/justice-league-international-returns-011012.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100115041552/http://www.newsarama.com/comics/justice-league-international-returns-011012.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 15, 2010 |title=JUSTICE LEAGUE INTERNATIONAL Returns in "GENERATION LOST" |publisher=[[Newsarama]] |date=January 12, 2010 |access-date=January 12, 2010}}</ref> Johns has discussed the general theme:

{{cquote|''Brightest Day'' is about second chances. I think it's been obvious from day one that there are major plans for the heroes and villains from ''[[Aquaman]]'' to take center stage in the DC Universe, among many others, post-Blackest Night. ''Brightest Day'' is not a banner or a vague catch-all direction for the DC Universe, it is a story. Nor is ''Brightest Day'' a sign that the DC Universe is going to be all about 'light and brighty' superheroes. Some second chances work out...some don't.<ref>{{cite web |first=Alex |last=Segura |url=http://dcu.blog.dccomics.com/2010/02/11/your-first-look-at-brightest-day-what-does-it-mean/ |title=Your first look at BRIGHTEST DAY — what does it mean? |work=The Source |publisher=DC Comics.com |date=February 11, 2010 |access-date=February 11, 2010}}</ref>}}

''Brightest Day'' also crossed over into the ''[[Green Lantern (comic book)|Green Lantern]]'' series, the ''[[Green Lantern Corps]]'', ''[[Justice League of America]]'', ''[[Teen Titans|The Titans]]'' and ''[[The Flash (comic book)|The Flash]]''.<ref>{{cite web |first=Lucas |last=Siegel |url=http://www.newsarama.com/comics/Brightest-Day-Announcement-100111.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113233126/http://www.newsarama.com/comics/Brightest-Day-Announcement-100111.html |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 13, 2010 |title=UPDATE 4: DC's BRIGHTEST DAY w/ David Finch! |publisher=[[Newsarama]] |date=January 11, 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010}}</ref> [[Gail Simone]] returned to a new volume of the ''[[Birds of Prey (team)|Birds of Prey]]'' comic book, which also went under the same banner.<ref>{{cite web|first=Brendan |last=McGuirk |url=http://www.comicsalliance.com/2010/01/13/gail-simone-returns-to-birds-of-prey/ |title=Gail Simone Returns to 'Birds of Prey' in 2010 -- EXCLUSIVE |publisher=[[ComicsAlliance]] |date=January 13, 2010 |access-date=January 13, 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100116103835/http://www.comicsalliance.com/2010/01/13/gail-simone-returns-to-birds-of-prey |archive-date=January 16, 2010}}</ref> Other tie-ins included the first issues of a relaunched ''[[Green Arrow]]'' and the ''[[Justice Society of America]]''. [[Jeff Lemire]] wrote the [[One-shot (comics)|one-shot]] ''Brightest Day: The [[Atom (Ray Palmer)|Atom]] Special'' with artist [[Mahmud Asrar]], which acted as a springboard for an Atom story to co-feature in ''[[Adventure Comics]]'' with the same creative team.<ref>{{cite web |first=Jeffrey |last=Renaud |url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=25682 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100415004809/http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=25682 |url-status=dead |archive-date=April 15, 2010 |title=Lemire Embiggens Ray Palmer |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=April 13, 2010 |access-date=April 13, 2010}}</ref>

The ''Green Lantern'' series featured more of the characters [[Atrocitus]], [[Larfleeze]], [[Saint Walker]], and [[Indigo Tribe#Prominent members|Indigo-1]] in a story arc titled "New Guardians".<ref>{{cite web |first=Jeffrey |last=Renaud |url=http://www.comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=24359 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100113041451/http://comicbookresources.com/?page=article&id=24359 |url-status=dead |archive-date=January 13, 2010 |title=GEOFF JOHNS PRIME: "Earth One", "Blackest Night" & More |publisher=[[Comic Book Resources]] |date=January 11, 2010 |access-date=January 11, 2010}}</ref> Johns said that [[Firestorm (character)|Firestorm]] is a "main character" in ''Brightest Day''.<ref name="Hudson">{{cite web|url=http://www.comicsalliance.com/2010/03/13/emerald-city-comic-con-the-dc-nation-panel/ |title=Emerald City Comic-Con: The DC Nation Panel |author=Hudson, Laura |date=March 13, 2010 |publisher=[[ComicsAlliance]] |access-date=2010-03-28 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110103172017/http://www.comicsalliance.com/2010/03/13/emerald-city-comic-con-the-dc-nation-panel/ |archive-date=January 3, 2011}}</ref>

The first issue, issue #0, was penciled by [[Fernando Pasarin]].<ref name="Melrose">{{cite web|url= http://robot6.comicbookresources.com/2010/01/dc-announces-blackest-night-followup-brightest-day/|title= DC announces Blackest Night follow-up: Brightest Day|author= Melrose, Kevin|date= January 11, 2010|work= Robot 6|publisher= [[Comic Book Resources]]|access-date= 2010-01-13|archive-date= 2012-05-12|archive-url= https://web.archive.org/web/20120512114813/http://robot6.comicbookresources.com/2010/01/dc-announces-blackest-night-followup-brightest-day/|url-status= dead}}</ref> [[David Finch (comics)|David Finch]], a newly DC exclusive artist, illustrated the covers for the entire series.<ref name="Melrose" />

''Brightest Day'' event was also used to introduce '''[[Jackson Hyde]]''', the new [[Aqualad]] created for the ''[[Young Justice (TV series)|Young Justice]]'' animated series, into the DC Universe.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://dcu.blog.dccomics.com/2010/06/15/opening-the-vault-%E2%80%93-a-live-action-blue-beetle/ |title=DC Universe: The Source » Blog Archive » OPENING THE VAULT – A LIVE-ACTION BLUE BEETLE? |work=Dcu.blog.dccomics.com |date=2010-06-15 |access-date=2011-02-06}}</ref> Similarly, the final issue reintroduces [[Swamp Thing]] and [[John Constantine]] into the mainstream DC Universe after their extended time in DC's ''[[Vertigo Comics]]'' imprint.

== Titles ==
* '''''Brightest Day''''' #0-24 (twice monthly, 25 issues including issue #0) focuses on the resurrected [[Deadman (character)|Deadman]], [[Hawkman]], [[Hawkgirl]], [[Martian Manhunter]], [[Aquaman]], and [[Firestorm (character)|Firestorm]].
* '''''[[Green Lantern (comic book)|Green Lantern]]''''' (vol. 4) #53-62 focuses on [[Hal Jordan]], as well as the other representatives of the other Lantern Corps, as they attempt to prevent the capture of all the emotional entities which eventually leads to the Green Lantern Corps War.
* '''''[[Green Lantern Corps]]''''' (vol. 2) #47-57 focuses on [[Kyle Rayner]], [[John Stewart (character)|John Stewart]], and [[Ganthet]] as they face the revolt of the [[Alpha Lanterns]] and the return of the [[Weaponers of Qward]] until the War of the Green Lantern Corps erupts.
* '''''Green Lantern: Emerald Warriors''''' (issues #1-6) focuses on [[Guy Gardner (character)|Guy Gardner]], [[Kilowog]], [[Arisia Rrab]], [[Sodam Yat]], and [[Bleez]] as they battle [[Krona (character)|Krona]] to prevent the War of the Green Lantern Corps.
* '''''Brightest Day: The Atom Special''''' is a one-shot that was bannered as a ''Brightest Day'' tie-in, but is in actuality an introduction to the Atom miniseries contained within ''[[Adventure Comics]]'' #516-521 and ''Giant-Size Atom'' #1.
* '''''[[Birds of Prey (team)|Birds of Prey]]''''' (vol. 2) #1-6 focuses on the resurrected [[Hank Hall|Hawk]] as well as the [[Hawk and Dove|Dove]]'s connection to the White Light.
* '''''[[The Flash (comic book)|The Flash]]''''' (vol. 3) #1-7 features the resurrected [[Captain Boomerang]].
* '''''[[Green Arrow]]''''' (vol. 4) #1-12 focuses on the Star City forest that sprouted from the White Lantern ring.
* '''''[[Justice League|Justice League of America]]''''' (vol. 3) #44-48 focuses on the resurrected Jade as she tries to save her brother [[Obsidian (character)|Obsidian]] and father [[Alan Scott]] from the control of the Starheart.
* '''''[[Justice League: Generation Lost]]''''' #1-24 (twice monthly, 24 issues) focuses on [[Booster Gold]], [[Captain Atom]], [[Fire (character)|Fire]], and [[Ice (character)|Ice]] as they attempt to find the resurrected [[Maxwell Lord]].
* '''''[[Justice Society of America]]''''' (vol. 3) #40-43, which is part of the storyline shared with ''[[Justice League of America]]'' #44-48.
* '''''[[Teen Titans#Titans (vol. 2) (2008–2011)|Titans]]''''' (vol. 2) #24-30 focuses on the resurrected [[Osiris (DC Comics)|Osiris]] as he joins a team of villains led by [[Deathstroke]], and composed of the [[Tattooed Man]], [[Cheshire (character)|Cheshire]], and a new character named ''Cinder''. An additional special called '''''Titans: Villains For Hire Special''''' #1 precedes number #24 and deals with the death of [[Atom (Ryan Choi)|Ryan Choi]], the fourth [[Atom (character)|Atom]], at the hands of the villains. For unknown reasons, issue #28 was the last issue to be labeled as a ''Brightest Day'' tie-in.

=== Involved, but not listed, under the ''Brightest Day'' banner ===
* '''''[[Action Comics]]''''' (beginning with issue #890–900) focuses on [[Lex Luthor]] and his universal quest to locate the energy of the [[Black Lantern Corps]]. Incidentally, issue #890 was labeled as ''[[Blackest Night]] Aftermath''.
* '''''[[Booster Gold]]''''' (vol. 2) #33–43 picks up on elements of the search for [[Maxwell Lord]] in ''[[Justice League: Generation Lost]]''.
* '''''[[Power Girl]]''''' #13–23 is loosely connected with ''[[Justice League: Generation Lost]]''.
* '''''[[Blackest Night#Blackest Night 2|Untold Tales from Blackest Night]]''''' #1 (October 2010): while it was labeled as "[[Blackest Night]]", this one-shot is loosely connected with ''Brightest Day'' #11–12, ''[[Green Lantern]]'' #59, and ''[[Green Arrow]]'' #5, all of which involve the return of the [[Black Lantern Corps]].
* '''''Green Lantern: Larfleeze Christmas Special''''': while not bannered as a "Brightest Day" tie-in, this issue is a tongue-in-cheek one-shot issue focusing on Larfleeze's misunderstanding of the meaning of Christmas.
* '''''[[Captain Marvel Jr.|Shazam!]]''''' #1: this one-shot is loosely connected with Osiris' mission to rescue his sister Isis.
* '''''[[Teen Titans]]''''' (vol. 3) #83 explains why [[Blue Beetle (Jaime Reyes)|Blue Beetle]] would be taking a leave of absence from the Titans, and the events of ''Generation Lost'' #2 are indirectly mentioned there as well.
* '''''[[War of the Green Lanterns]]''''' is a storyline that crosses over all three Green Lantern titles, and is a direct continuation of the "Brightest Day" story arcs (''Green Lantern'' #63-67, ''Green Lantern Corps'' #58-60, ''Green Lantern: Emerald Warriors'' #7-10 and ''War of the Green Lanterns: Aftermath'' #1-2).

== ''Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search for Swamp Thing'' ==
In June, a three-issue miniseries involved the return of [[John Constantine]] to the [[DC Universe]] and his attempt to convince [[Superman]] and [[Batman]] that the choosing of Alec Holland (the new [[Swamp Thing]]) as the Earth's new protector is inevitable and the resurrected Alec Holland will have to die, so that his soul can merge again with the Green.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Parkin |first=JK |date=2011-05-04 |title=DC Comics releases full cover for ''Search for Swamp Thing'' |url=http://robot6.comicbookresources.com/2011/05/dc-comics-releases-full-cover-for-search-for-swamp-thing/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120811010705/http://robot6.comicbookresources.com/2011/05/dc-comics-releases-full-cover-for-search-for-swamp-thing/ |archive-date=2012-08-11 |access-date=2011-05-07 |work=[[Comic Book Resources]] |language=en}}</ref>

* ''Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search for Swamp Thing'' #1, 32 pages, June 22, 2011<ref>{{cite web |first=Jonathan |last=Vankin |url=http://dccomics.com/dcu/comics/?cm=18338 |title=DCU Comics - Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search #1 (of 3) |publisher=[[DC Comics.com]] |access-date=April 16, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140927071346/http://www.dccomics.com/comics/brightest-day-aftermath-the-search-2011/brightest-day-aftermath-the-search-1 |archive-date=September 27, 2014}}</ref>
* ''Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search for Swamp Thing'' #2, 32 pages, July 27, 2011<ref>{{cite web |first=Jonathan |last=Vankin |url=http://dccomics.com/dcu/comics/?cm=18974 |title=DCU Comics - Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search #2 (of 3) |publisher=[[DC Comics.com]] |access-date=April 16, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130721021524/http://www.dccomics.com/comics/brightest-day-aftermath-the-search-2011/brightest-day-aftermath-the-search-2 |archive-date=July 21, 2013}}</ref>
* ''Brightest Day Aftermath: The Search for Swamp Thing'' #3, 32 pages, August 24, 2011
